races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Grainne A Chroi
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on soft last time and has placed form on good ground too — this trip and surface suit, and Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a meaningful weight concession; will be prominent throughout and is the value threat to the Mullins pair.|

runners_data.name: Murcia
runners_data.note: Paul Townend's booking for Mullins' five-year-old is the standout angle; won over 16f on good most recently and the step up to 2m4½f looks a logical progression — prominent style fits the race shape perfectly and the tongue tie is noted.|

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form including a win 12 days ago makes this a live contender on fitness, but Elliott's five-year-old is a genuine pace-seeker whose natural position at the front is denied here by the stronger prominent claims of Birdie Or Bust, Murcia and Grainne A Chroi — forced to race off the pace, which blunts its best chance.|

runners_data.name: Diamond Du Berlais
runners_data.note: Mullins' hold-up horse has a course win over 21f on soft but good-ground form reads poorly (sim-going 0W0P in 2 runs) — Brian Hayes will have to come from behind into a race not set up to be run slowly, making this a tough assignment.|

runners_data.name: Run For Mahler
runners_data.note: Two wins on good ground over shorter trips show ability, but Byrnes' seven-year-old is a front-runner by nature and with Birdie Or Bust firmly in control of the lead, Enright will find himself racing in unfamiliar territory further back than ideal — style fit is compromised.|

runners_data.name: Birdie Or Bust
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's eight-year-old is the confirmed pace-setter and Cobden's ability to manage the gallop is central to the race shape; style fit score reflects that winning from the front requires more than just setting the pace — needs to quicken clear when challenged, which good-ground form of 2W4P in 15 runs suggests is far from certain.|

runners_data.name: Taketwotoone
runners_data.note: 189 days off the track and a sequence of finishing positions no better than 8th in the last five runs paints a bleak picture; amateur-ridden hold-up horse flagged as likely to fade in the finish, and the evidence strongly supports treating this as a non-factor.|

races.paceDynamic: Birdie Or Bust is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing to contest the lead, Harry Cobden's mount should dictate on its own terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m4½f trip on good ground. Grainne A Chroi and Murcia will push forward into prominent positions just off the leader, creating a small group in front while the hold-up horses — Diamond Du Berlais and Taketwotoone — settle in rear. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the pace map can accommodate; Run For Mahler and Ardeen Joy are genuine pace-seeking horses who will be squeezed into midfield roles they don't naturally occupy, limiting their effectiveness. With Birdie Or Bust able to control tempo without pressure, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in a small leading group and quicken from the front when the race begins in earnest approaching the final two flights — prominent-to-lead profiles are the clear tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Group Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Birdie Or Bust dictates an uncontested gallop and the race is won from the front two or three.
scenarios.body: Cobden settles Birdie Or Bust into a rhythm with Murcia and Grainne A Chroi tracking closely, and the race is decided among this small group as stamina and class tell in the closing stages; the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up on a sound surface with no pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Class Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If Birdie Or Bust quickens early enough to string the field out, exposing gaps that a horse from behind can exploit with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: Diamond Du Berlais, Mullins' hold-up type on a rare good-ground start, finds the tempo insufficient to stop a late run if the front group get too comfortable and ties up; this scenario hinges on the leaders burning more energy than it appears, which is unlikely but possible over 2m4½f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Birdie Or Bust goes too fast early or makes a jumping error that disrupts rhythm and the pace unravels.
scenarios.body: A misjudged gallop or costly mistake at a flight could allow the backmarkers to close the gap rapidly in the straight; Diamond Du Berlais and Taketwotoone are the only true hold-up types but Taketwotoone's poor recent form and long layoff (189 days) make it an unlikely beneficiary even in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Pair Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed horses Run For Mahler and Ardeen Joy manage to secure closer positions than mapped and the pace is genuinely strong.
scenarios.body: Both are natural front-runners shuffled back, and if they can find daylight and recover their preferred spots by halfway they could be competitive; however, racing out of their natural role compromises their chance significantly and this scenario is the least structurally supported.

watchPoints.text: Murcia has Paul Townend in the saddle for Mullins with an in-form trainer strike rate (3/26 in 14 days) — watch for this one to be ridden prominently and challenge Birdie Or Bust from two flights out.

Birdie Or Bust's jumping must be monitored closely — any mistake on the lead could instantly reshape the race and bring the hold-up horses back into contention in what is otherwise a front-runner's race.

Ardeen Joy ran just 12 days ago and returns fit, but watch whether Sam Ewing can work forward to a more natural position in the early stages — if so, its recent winning form makes it more dangerous than the midfield mapping suggests.

Diamond Du Berlais is worth tracking from the rear as the race enters the final mile; if the pace is even modest and the front group begins to tie up, Brian Hayes will be angling for a run — the 77-day absence and poor good-ground record temper expectations but Mullins' horses rarely run without a plan.

Taketwotoone's 189-day absence and consistently poor finishing positions make it a significant non-runner in practical terms — if it suddenly travels well early, treat that as a pace warning for the rest of the field.

races.name: D. Ivo O'Sullivan Memorial Irish EBF Mares Hurdle

runners_data.name: Amina
runners_data.note: Consistent prominently-run mare with four places from five runs on good ground; six-year-old for John McConnell who knows this trip well, and a clean jumping record makes her a solid each-way proposition in a chaotic field.

runners_data.name: Be My Fortune
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott hold-up runner who fades in the finish — 54 days off and a single good-ground run on record showing an eighth; the fade flag and lack of recent form make it hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Cool Native
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott prominent type who has won at around this trip; third on good ground last time, though 95 days off is a concern in a competitive mares' hurdle; the placed run on good in her history offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for C Byrnes who has been placing with metronomic regularity — five runs, three seconds or thirds — but has yet to win; prominently ridden over a variety of ground types with strong recent activity (27 days since last run).

runners_data.name: Dunaird
runners_data.note: Lightly raced seven-year-old for Eugene O'Sullivan with an unknown going profile making assessment difficult; the trainer has no recent runners to draw on (0/0 in 14 days), and an unclassified style means she is one of the bigger unknowns here.

runners_data.name: Early Dawning
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins prominent runner returning from 196 days off — a significant concern; two runs on record, both placed or thereabouts, but the long layoff in this company is a major red flag regardless of the yard.

runners_data.name: Eyecanboogie
runners_data.note: E McNamara runner with an unclassified style and a P-0-6 recent form string suggesting no clear winning thread; good ground form is patchy (third from four runs) and this looks a competitive assignment.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won last time on good ground (1m6f flat win) but whose jumping form over hurdles is limited and placed returns are modest; Paul Flynn yard is active (4/25 in 14 days) and the nine-day turnaround needs monitoring.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton hold-up runner whose sole hurdle run produced an eleventh on good ground; the fade-in-finish flag compounded by that raw form makes this a very difficult profile to support.

runners_data.name: Happy Me
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose best recent effort was a third at 3/19f on soft-ish ground; most hurdle form has come on heavier ground and the going switch to good is a mild question mark over the trip.

runners_data.name: Individualism
runners_data.note: E McNamara hold-up type whose flat form includes a pair of wins but whose hurdle record (sixth from one run) and difficult-going history makes her an extreme risk in a 24-runner field on good ground.

runners_data.name: Joly Saphir
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton runner flagged as lightly raced with no going profile or last run date available — virtually impossible to assess from available data alone; treat as a speculative outsider.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Donncha Duggan's runner carries strong hold-up credentials in a race where the rear is already crowded; with 200 days off and a poor recent form string, this is one occasion where the style fit and absence make the chances slim regardless of repositioning.

runners_data.name: Marble Rile
runners_data.note: Norman Lee hold-up runner whose single hurdle run delivered a thirteenth on good ground; the fade flag makes this a bottom-of-the-market profile with no obvious route to competitiveness.

runners_data.name: Market Ready
runners_data.note: Sean Aherne prominent mare with consistent placed form (four places from seven good/similar runs) over 2m; stepping up in trip here is a legitimate question but she knows how to race and the profile suits a steadily-run contest.

runners_data.name: Martin Plage
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins prominent type returning from 589 days off — by far the longest absence in this field; placed form on soft largely irrelevant to today's conditions, and the rust from nearly 20 months away is an enormous handicap.

runners_data.name: Mister Killeens
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery unclassified four-year-old whose four career runs have all produced mid-to-lower finishes across varied ground; youth and inconsistency make this a very speculative runner in such a large field.

runners_data.name: Roll It Roisin
runners_data.note: David Harry Kelly runner with an unknown going profile and minimal form (P-5 recent record); lightly raced flag and no last-run date available make this among the hardest to evaluate in the race.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell hold-up mare whose two good-ground runs produced a seventeenth and a sixth — modest recent profile; finished well in a bumper-esque flat win but the hurdles record offers nothing to build on.

runners_data.name: Spring Waltz
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead prominent mare who placed second on good ground last time (2m3f); recent return of just 33 days shows freshness, and the trainer's 5/35 in-form record adds confidence — this profile suits a steadily-run race off a single pacesetter.

runners_data.name: Tippawan Haa
runners_data.note: Terence O'Brien prominent type who was second on good ground at 2m2f and has a pair of placed efforts; 89 days off is a mild concern but the distance and going appear within her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Tis Well For Some
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's confirmed front-runner who is likely to get a soft lead in the absence of any pressing rivals; the style-fit caveat is noted but in a 24-runner field no one else is going to lead, so she inherits the role by default.

runners_data.name: Tyson Fury
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan prominent mare who has placed twice recently — including a second at 2m1f on good ground — with a long career record suggesting she retains ability at nine; the shorter flat-win profile is slightly at odds with today's trip but she is competitive.

runners_data.name: Whitehall Girl
runners_data.note: E McNamara four-year-old flagged as lightly raced with no last-run date or going profile; the yard is cold (0/10 in 14 days) and there is simply not enough data to form a confident view.

races.paceDynamic: Tis Well For Some is the one confirmed front-runner in a 24-runner field and, though tagged with a style-fit caveat, is likely to get to the front unchallenged given the prominent types — Amina, Spring Waltz, Cool Native, Dawn Coming, Early Dawning and Martin Plage — will be jostling for position rather than disputing the lead outright. With only one genuine pace-setter, the tempo over 2m4½f on good ground is likely to be sustainable and controlled rather than searching, which compresses the race into the final half-mile rather than stringing it out. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can cleanly accommodate: Luck Between Us is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map, and among the prominent brigade it is Spring Waltz and Amina who look best-placed to actually secure a position close to the pace given their recent form and handler strength. The controlled, single-pace-setter scenario hands the clearest tactical advantage to prominent racers who can track the leader without burning energy — a seat just off Tis Well For Some's shoulder into the straight is the prime real estate here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tis Well For Some dictates a steady tempo and the prominent chasers track neatly without scrimmaging.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds at a measured gallop with Spring Waltz, Amina or Cool Native sitting a length or two off the lead, conserving energy before striking turning for home; on good ground at this trip, horses who travel comfortably in the first three are rarely overtaken by closers when the pace has been modest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front-Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop proves genuinely honest as the prominent pack pushes Tis Well For Some along and the tempo strings the field out.
scenarios.body: With 24 runners funnelling into hurdles, early barging could force a faster-than-expected pace, which would suit a front-runner able to build a cushion; Tis Well For Some, if running freely in a clear lead, could find the honest pace ironically suiting it by spreading the field and removing late threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners use each other up fighting for position and genuine ground is lost up front in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Forlio has winning form on good ground and covers a lot of ground from hold-up; Tyson Fury has placed twice recently at around this distance and possesses the finishing speed to pick up a tired field — though most true closers are hampered by the large field and likely traffic through the final bend.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos Rules
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, unseated riders or a blanket scrimmage at hurdles disrupts the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: In a 24-runner mares' hurdle, interference is a live risk and a chaotic early pace can throw the form book out entirely; horses with clean jumping records and the ability to switch off in traffic — Amina, who has placed consistently, or Early Dawning stepping back from a long absence — could benefit from simply getting round safely.

watchPoints.text: Watch for scrimmaging at the early hurdles — with 24 runners in a mares' hurdle, Dunaird, Eyecanboogie and Mister Killeens are unclassified types without established jumping form who could cause interference.

Martin Plage returns from 589 days off for Willie Mullins — a horse running cold after nearly 20 months could be a loose cannon in a crowded early-race scenario and should be monitored for erratic jumping.

Luck Between Us arrives after 200 days off and is a genuine hold-up horse forced further forward by the field composition — watch for it being caught wide or short of room on the final bend if pace quickens unexpectedly.

Early Dawning's 196-day layoff for Mullins means she may be ring-rusty in a large-field environment; prominent types who lose their position early in this field shape face a very hard task clawing back ground.

Be My Fortune and Grabat both carry a fade-in-finish flag — if either is prominent into the straight they are worth opposing rather than supporting, as the closing stages of 2m4½f on good ground will expose that weakness.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Swelltime
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer rated 100 who fades when the pace quickens sharply — the fade flag is a concern, and 14 days since last run is not an issue, but finishing form in similar going (1W2P from 12) suggests limited upside at the trip here.|

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: 200 days off the track is a significant layoff flag for this 6-year-old, and the trainer's 0/3 in 14 days suggests no strong current form — hold-up style suits a true staying test but the long absence makes confidence hard.|

runners_data.name: Malikanna
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this race and the pace-maker by default, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) hints it is operating at the outer edge of its comfort zone at this trip — its best form has come over shorter; watch whether it is allowed to control fully.|

runners_data.name: King Ferdinand
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old prominent racer with a strong good-ground profile (3W5P similar going) who has form over 2m+ distances — the age is a flag but the class record at this OR band and prominent style suit this scenario well.|

runners_data.name: Papagei
runners_data.note: Ran just four days ago which is a major fitness/freshness concern for a hurdler at this distance — hold-up style could spare it early, but the quick reappearance at 2m4½f on good ground is hard to forgive.|

runners_data.name: Gaoithe Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (t) that has not won on good ground in five similar-going starts — the zero-wins-zero-places on good in the sim-going record is a blunt fact that limits confidence despite a tidy handicap mark.|

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with 4 wins from 13 on good ground and a win over 23f — the headgear (p) has featured in placed efforts; the 14-day turnaround is fine and this profile suits the expected race shape directly.|

runners_data.name: Koeur A Prendre
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose natural position is further back than the map shows — the redistribution is purely positional congestion; its recent second on good ground over 2m is the standout piece of form but gets back further than ideal in a big field.|

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: Form figures of 800P-P tell a bleak story for this 4-year-old, and the hold-up style has not delivered — sim-going form is sparse (3 runs) with no placed efforts; hard to recommend at any position.|

runners_data.name: Brianna Lily
runners_data.note: A genuine back-marker by inclination placed into the midfield graphic by congestion alone — the nine-year-old has placed twice on good ground, and the 31-day break is manageable, but finishing form has been inconsistent.|

runners_data.name: Boston Queen
runners_data.note: Trained by the in-form Gordon Elliott yard (10/68 in 14 days) but the fade flag and a form string of 9960-B on good ground are alarming — displaced from its natural hold-up berth by the field size, its actual record on this surface is five runs, zero placed.|

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose entire recent form has come over 2m2f+ on good ground (14/15 runs), so the trip is familiar, but eight placed finishes without a win from 15 similar-going starts tells of a willing grinder who cannot quite land the blow.|

runners_data.name: Tedworth
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 2m on its last win and has consistent placed form over this trip — the hold-up style is genuine and the sim-going record of 15/15 good-ground runs is thorough experience; pushed into midfield by congestion but a legitimate finisher.|

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: Non-runner status means this horse will not participate — any scenario that relied on its presence is moot, and its absence removes one fade-flagged hold-up type from the back-marker congestion.|

runners_data.name: Pleasureofpressure
runners_data.note: Trainer Rothwell 2/21 in 14 days — solid recent activity; prominent racer whose form string 4234-4 shows a horse that consistently places and stays competitive from the front group, which is exactly what this race shape rewards.|

runners_data.name: Miss Donna
runners_data.note: Lower-rated prominent type stepping up from 16f/17f distances to 2m4½f, which is a significant trip question — the headgear (t) is worn for the first time, and the 41-day break is fine, but the step in distance is the key watchpoint.|

races.paceDynamic: Malikanna is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and is likely to bowl along uncontested at the head of affairs, setting a genuine but sustainable gallop over 2m4½f on good ground. Inchidaly Copper, King Ferdinand, Pleasureofpressure and Miss Donna are legitimate prominent types who will push forward and track closely, ensuring the early tempo is not dawdling even if Malikanna dictates. The redistribution note is important here: Koeur A Prendre, Brianna Lily, Boston Queen, Mother Ship, Tedworth and Beacon Bypass are all genuine hold-up horses by nature but are pushed into the midfield graphic because the field holds far more back-markers than the map can accommodate at the rear — Koeur A Prendre and Brianna Lily are most likely to actually secure a position nearer the pace given the congestion. With one pace-setter and a cluster of prominent trackers, this sets up as a steady-to-fair gallop that will develop into a staying test from the second-last — a race shape that historically favours experienced, honest prominent horses or hold-up types with proven stamina who can quicken from a handy position, rather than deep closers who must make up ground from a disadvantaged spot in traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Malikanna Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Malikanna bowls along unchallenged and the prominent tracking horses Inchidaly Copper, King Ferdinand and Pleasureofpressure sit within two lengths throughout.
scenarios.body: Malikanna sets a measured pace and the race develops into a sustained grind from the second-last, suiting horses who have been travelling comfortably in behind and can quicken off a decent gallop; Inchidaly Copper's strong good-ground form over this sort of trip and Pleasureofpressure's consistent placed record make them ideal beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to string out the field and a genuine hold-up horse picks its way through beaten rivals in the straight.
scenarios.body: Koeur A Prendre showed a sharp finishing effort last time at 2m on good ground and, if it can find a clear run from midfield, its natural hold-up profile suits a race where the leaders have burned through their reserves; Tedworth's winning form over this course and distance configuration also gives it a strong profile here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies the Field
scenarios.trigger: If Malikanna is allowed a completely uncontested lead at a low enough gallop to conserve energy and simply outstay the field.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to force the issue from flagfall, Malikanna could effectively control the tempo entirely and arrive at the last with reserves intact; the STYLE_FIT tag is a discount, but in a race where back-markers are not true closers, the front-runner stealing the race from the front becomes a credible alternate shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Traffic, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the large 16-runner field creates messy early positioning and traffic problems that allow a lightly-weighted or improving horse to emerge through the carnage.
scenarios.body: Miss Donna and Gaoithe Glory, both lower in the weights and capable of finding a clear passage on the inner, could benefit if the fancied hold-up horses are blocked; with many horses racing out of their natural position, an unexposed or lightly-raced type capable of tracking the pace smoothly could capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Beacon Bypass is a non-runner — confirm declaration status early as it affects field size and any betting markets built around the pace map.

Malikanna's front-running role is unchallenged, but its STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) and shorter-trip form mean it could find this 2m4½f test at the limits of its stamina — watch if it weakens sharply from the second-last.

Papagei ran just four days ago — monitor whether connections have declared it fit; a quick turnaround at this trip on good ground often produces a below-par effort from hurdlers and could cause interference if it tires mid-race.

Luck Between Us returns from a 200-day absence — horses off that long in jumps handicaps frequently need the run, and in a 16-runner field it poses a potential jumping hazard especially if it drops out tamely in the back straight.

The large field of 16 with multiple displaced hold-up types (Koeur A Prendre, Tedworth, Brianna Lily, Mother Ship) clustered in midfield creates significant traffic risk at the top of the straight — runners on the outside or with a clear passage early will have a structural advantage.

races.name: Noel C. Duggan Structural Steel 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tuche De Houelle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with limited data points; only two hurdle runs in her history and a best of fourth over this trip on good ground, which makes her difficult to assess with confidence — unknown running style adds further opacity.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old front-runner for Gavin Cromwell who has strong form at 18f on good ground; leads with a STYLE_FIT note of 0.92 suggesting he is operating slightly outside his ideal mode here, but confirmed pace role makes him the race-shaper regardless.

runners_data.name: Global Skies
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan runner with two wins from three runs at 20f on good ground — the trip and conditions are demonstrably in his favour; a genuine prominent runner who should secure a front-rank position and arrives with strong recent form (211).

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old carrying unknown going preference and 133 days off the track; in form showing a run of 3046- and a hurdle/chase mix in headgear, making him one of the harder horses to place tactically — a blank slate with real uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Kazakh d'Arthel
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second string who won over 18f on good ground but has been beaten on his last five outings including a fall; sim-going record of 9 wins/15 runs suggests good ground suits him, though his 0 from 5 recent form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Only For Our Man
runners_data.note: Consistent Paul Nolan runner who has finished placed in four of five recent starts, including a win over 22f on good ground; handles this trip well and his prominent style is well-suited to tracking Arcland into the straight.

runners_data.name: Market Ready
runners_data.note: Arrives on the back of a fourth from five runs at 16f on various ground, all at the shorter end of his trip range; a natural front-runner whose chance is tempered by being mapped towards the rear end of the field — not his preferred way of racing.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's nine-year-old ran only four days ago and has a solid record at 22-26f on good ground with seven career placings; his true prominent style is squeezed by the front-heavy field and being mapped to midfield is a genuine disadvantage rather than a natural fit.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Two wins at 18-19f on good ground for Cian Collins, and arrives in form after back-to-back placings; a natural front-runner who will struggle to access his preferred position given the congestion ahead of him — the redistribution to midfield is a real cost to his chance.

runners_data.name: Speakasyoufind
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying a finishing-fade flag and a recent run of 80P-92; despite two runs at 20f on good ground the flagged fade tendency undermines any late-run scenario, making this a difficult race shape for her to win from the back.

races.paceDynamic: Arcland is the one confirmed front-runner here and is likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset, setting a sustainable, uncontested tempo over the 2m4½f trip on good ground. Global Skies, Kazakh d'Arthel, and Only For Our Man will push for prominent positions just off the pace, creating a bunched front rank but without the genuine pressure that would turn this into a true test of stamina from an early stage. Speakasyoufind is the sole genuine hold-up horse, though a finishing fade flag undermines her late-race credentials. This race shape favours horses who can track Arcland in a close-up prominent position and pick off the leader in the home straight — a controlled, front-running tempo with a modest prominent pack behind it is the dominant shape, and horses who can travel just off the pace without expending energy early hold the clearest tactical advantage. The field also holds more prominent types than can all secure that position: Global Skies and Kazakh d'Arthel are best-placed to claim the front-rank slots, while Smallcraftwarning and Blue Reed — both natural prominent racers — are likely to find themselves shuffled wider and further back than they would prefer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arcland Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Arcland dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the race is decided by who can quicken from just off the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Arcland leads at a fair clip but is never seriously challenged for position, leaving the prominent trackers fresh enough to mount a challenge from two out; Global Skies and Only For Our Man, both proven at this trip on good ground, are ideally placed to accelerate past a potentially tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Arcland's uncontested lead proves decisive and the pace is slow enough that no closer can generate enough momentum to overhaul.
scenarios.body: A sedate early gallop gifts Arcland an energy advantage, and with no horse applying pressure at any stage, the lead is never meaningfully threatened until it is too late for the prominent chasers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quick enough to string out the field and Smallcraftwarning or Blue Reed, despite being pushed wider than ideal, manage to produce a late run.
scenarios.body: Both horses are natural prominent types racing out of role and would need an unusually strong pace to set up a late finish; this scenario is structurally undermined by their redistribution to midfield, making it a low-probability shape reliant on things going wrong for the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group becomes congested or there are jumping errors that disrupt the front rank, opening a gap for a lightly-raced or unknown quantity.
scenarios.body: Tuche De Houelle or Jupiter Du Gite, both with uncertain profiles and unknown or lightly-tested credentials, could benefit from a messy race that nullifies the pace map entirely; the lightly-raced flag on both makes them unpredictable wild cards rather than genuine pace-map beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Smallcraftwarning and Blue Reed are both natural front-runners who may attempt to push forward early despite being mapped to midfield — any scramble for prominent positions could disrupt the pace plan and cause interference in the first mile.

Jupiter Du Gite has been off the track for 133 days and his running style is entirely unknown — watch for him running green or jumping poorly on his first outing back, which could cause problems for horses tracking him.

Speakasyoufind is flagged as a horse who fades in the finish; if she is in contention turning for home and suddenly weakens, horses attempting to follow her run could find themselves blocked or carried wide at a critical moment.

Arcland's STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 indicates a slight positional mismatch — if he fails to lead as expected or is outpaced to the front by one of the other prominent types, the entire pace map shifts and the scenario probabilities recalibrate significantly.

Tuche De Houelle and Market Ready both have limited recent form at this trip and course; their headgear (hg:t and hg:t respectively) is worth noting as tongue-tie runners can produce unexpectedly strong or unusually erratic efforts when conditions align.

races.name: Kerry Drains Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kamino Bello
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Gavin Cromwell who won over 18f on good ground last time; the 32-day break looks fine, but the OR of 113 gives him the burden of top weight at 169lbs, and from off the pace in a field of closers he needs a dream run.|

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a strong record on good ground (1W2P from 8 runs), though 67 days off and a string of placed but non-winning efforts raises the question of whether he quite gets to the line; tongue-tie fitted and a genuine hold-up horse who needs things to set up late.|

runners_data.name: Kabylia
runners_data.note: A Cromwell-trained prominent racer who has placed at this sort of trip on good ground before; the hood is fitted and she maps as one of the natural stalkers of Secret Rock, meaning the race shape does not compromise her position — that's a meaningful edge in this field.|

runners_data.name: Secret Rock
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire pace template for this contest; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals this is not a natural lead role, and while the good-ground figures are acceptable, the absence of dominant front-running form over this trip should temper confidence beyond dictating terms.|

runners_data.name: Lips Freedom
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on soft last time out and arrives on a 109-day break; the fade-in-finish flag is a genuine concern in a race where the gallop could be steady and the final hurdle kicks everything into a sprint, making her dubious for place purposes.|

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Recent second over 16f on soft suggests he handles cut, but good ground here should suit; the 16-day turnaround is short, and jockey Dylan O'Connor claims 7lbs which helps offset the weight, with his hold-up style likely translating to a prominent enough position given field dynamics.|

runners_data.name: Katakana
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead sends out a horse who won over 16f on good ground but hasn't run in 244 days — the layoff is the dominant concern; a true hold-up type whose deepest instincts will be squeezed by the number of rivals wanting the same late ground, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.|

runners_data.name: Mc Swagger
runners_data.note: Unconventional runner who falls into the fade-in-finish category; five-year-old with no wins on good ground and a pulled-up effort in recent form, making it hard to construct a winning scenario even if the race shape were ideal.|

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: Ran 10 days ago and returns quickly for P A Fahy; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear, but in a field this congested with closers, he will be competing for the same late lanes and the 0W0P sim-going record offers little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Regards To Rose
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good ground and has place form in bigger fields, so the form profile is live; the 14-day turnaround is quick but not alarming, and his true hold-up instincts mean he will likely be further back than ideal — the STYLE_FIT flag is a real tactical handicap here.|

runners_data.name: Rattledelatch
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and no wins on good or heavy ground in the sim-going record; a true hold-up type who is over-represented at the back of this field and has not shown the ability to quicken through rivals when the gaps are tight.|

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: Won twice over 17f on good ground and placed three times in similar conditions, making the going profile one of the stronger in the race; the 13-day turnaround for P J Rothwell is brisk but the trainer has runners at a 2/21 clip recently, and while mapped to midfield, his natural style could see him land closer to the prominent bunch.|

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag allied to a 3/20f run on good ground as the best recent effort; the Andrew McNamara-trained six-year-old has poor sim-going stats (13/15) and the hold-up style in this crowded rear group makes a winning performance hard to envisage.|

runners_data.name: Kingdom Calling
runners_data.note: McCarthy runner returning 16 days after last start; fade-in-finish flag, no wins on good ground in the sim-going sample, and mapped well off the pace in a field where true hold-up horses already outnumber available cover — the profile is weak from multiple angles.|

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old returning from a 277-day absence for David Harry Kelly; has placed prominently over 20-24f on good ground in the past so the trip and going are not concerns, but the long break and age make fitness the overriding question, even if he maps as a natural prominent type with a decent pace position.|

races.paceDynamic: Secret Rock is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will slide into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front — sustainable enough to preserve energy for the final hill at Killarney. With only Kabylia and Corkbeg as natural prominent types to press forward, the tempo is likely to be honest but not searingly fast, which suits horses travelling within themselves in the first half of the race. The field is saturated with hold-up horses — Katakana, Regards To Rose, Home By The Sea, Kilt, Rattledelatch, Midnight Eagle and Kingdom Calling are all genuine closers pushed into midfield slots on the map because the rear is overpopulated — and the reality is that most of these will not achieve the deep-cover position their style demands. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, front-end gallop with one genuine pace-setter favours prominent racers who can travel in the first three or four, and hold-up horses who get shuffled towards the middle of the field rather than the back will be better placed than those trapped at the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Secret Rock Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Rock leads at a fair but uncontested clip and the field strings out on the run to the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Secret Rock dictates every yard, conserving enough to extend on the run-in, while Kabylia tracks closely and picks up the pieces if the leader tires; this shape punishes those with too much ground to make up from the rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Rock's pace proves just fast enough to stretch the field and a close-tracking horse pounces at the last.
scenarios.body: A horse like Party President or Kilt, travelling prominently or just off the pace, arrives at the final hurdle full of running and sustains the challenge to the line; the steady gallop means there is no wall of beaten horses to pass, rewarding those who bided their time just behind the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Rock's pace is genuinely slow early and the field bunches, allowing a hold-up horse to find daylight between the last two hurdles.
scenarios.body: A horse like Kamino Bello or Regards To Rose, sitting in a genuine mid-to-rear position and finding clear running, can pick off tiring front-runners on the climb to the line; this scenario requires the pace to be truly inadequate and room to present itself late, both of which are uncertain given the number of hold-up types crowding the same ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Overpresses, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Kabylia or another prominent type applies pressure to Secret Rock and the early gallop becomes ragged, causing an untidy race.
scenarios.body: Secret Rock, forced to race at a pace beyond its comfort zone, capitulates before the last and drags several midfield rivals into contention; a horse with tactical versatility such as Party President or Claude, who can adapt its position mid-race, would be best placed to capitalise on the resulting disorder.

watchPoints.text: Secret Rock's early sectionals are critical — if Kabylia or Corkbeg press forward to challenge the lead, Secret Rock may be asked to race faster than suits its profile and the entire front-running scenario collapses.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Katakana, Regards To Rose, Home By The Sea, Kilt, Rattledelatch) will all be fighting for the same ground on the run to the final hurdle — watch for a logjam on the inner that leaves several of them without a clear run.

Kamino Bello carries top weight of 169lbs and is partnered by a 5lb claimer; if Eoghan Finegan cannot find a clear passage early enough turning for home, the combination of weight and traffic could cost him at the business end.

Kilt's sim-going record (13/15 runs on good) is by far the deepest in the field for this surface — if the Killarney going turns out to be genuinely good, that experience edge over rivals with sparse turf form is worth monitoring in-running.

Corkbeg's 277-day absence demands an eye in the paddock — if he returns looking well within himself and travels prominently from the off, the class drop to OR 86 and proven good-ground form over staying trips makes him a potential each-way outsider to note.
